designDecision.s4_1b: Add plan_review_activity.atom_did (populate at the one call site that already resolves an atom -- GET /api/plan-review/code -- for free, no substrate dependency) and plan_review_activity.request_id (left NULL on every row; reserved for the true ledger correlation id, never filled with a plan-review-side substitute -- filling it with a value that can never match would read as an attempted match that silently always fails, which is worse than an honest absence). Add plan_review_activity.dedup_key, populated from a UUID minted once per inbound HTTP request in server.mjs and threaded through every recordActivity() call made while handling that request, enforced by a partial unique index (NULLs exempt, so pre-migration rows are unaffected). This gives real, DB-enforced protection against plan-review's own repeated-insert bug class; it does not and cannot protect against a client-side network retry, which arrives as a distinct request. New table plan_review_ledger_reconciliation records one append-only row per reconciliation pass (counts, divergence list, and an explicit basis string), so a reconciliation run is a durable record per ENFORCEMENT's 'state changing operations leave a record' rather than a transient response. A reconciliation pass attempts to fetch ledger rows via an MCP tool call (source_obligation_ledger_list -- does not exist on the server today, confirmed above); when the tool is absent the pass writes basis='blocked-no-reader-tool' honestly instead of reporting zero divergence, which would misrepresent 'never checked' as 'checked and clean'.
designDecision.s4_8: Reader lives in plan-review as GET /api/icc/obligations/reconciliation, sibling to the existing GET /api/icc/activity (same repo, same bearer-token gate already applied to every /api/icc/* and /api/plan-review/* route at the top of handle()). Reads the persisted plan_review_ledger_reconciliation rows plan-review already produced; does not attempt to mirror ledger content plan-review has no path to. Reasoning for placement, to satisfy the dispatch's 'note the reasoning in your close' instruction: (1) building it in hauska-mcp-server would be writing another seat's repo, which this dispatch's own out-of-scope line already forbids for S4-3/S4-7 and applies equally here; (2) the seam table row 'ICC paid across Smart Site AND Plan Review | one ledger' argues against a THIRD surface fragmenting an already-two-surface picture further; (3) plan-review already hosts the activity-cache audit precedent at /api/icc/activity, so this is a sibling of an existing pattern, not a new one. The true source-of-truth reader for the ledger itself still belongs on the substrate side eventually (naturally the next ask after S4-7); this reader surfaces what plan-review can honestly attest to about its own reconciliation attempts, not a mirror of substrate's data.

adversarialReview.selfChallenge1: Am I overstepping into substrate's repo by writing an MCP tool caller for a tool that does not exist? No: the call target is an HTTP tool-call to a deployed service, made from plan-review's own client code (src/mcp.mjs pattern), identical in shape to every other MCP call this repo already makes. No file in hauska-mcp-server is touched.
adversarialReview.selfChallenge2: Could I instead just add plan-review's own request id into the ledger's request_id column locally to get SOME match rate? Rejected: it would never actually correlate (the two ids are generated independently on each side), so it would report either 0 matches forever (indistinguishable from 'blocked') or, worse, look plausible while being meaningless. An honest blocked state is more useful to an auditor than a column that looks populated and correlates nothing.
adversarialReview.selfChallenge3: Is the dedup_key mechanism real or cosmetic? It is a genuine DB-enforced unique constraint, verified against a live scratch Postgres before shipping (see CP2). It is explicitly scoped to protect against plan-review's own duplicate-insert bug class, not client network retries -- that limitation is stated in the migration's own comment, not left implicit.
